title: Air India Express to Resume Direct Chandigarh–Sharjah Flights From October 26
excerpt: The four-times-weekly service, suspended since 2023, gives travellers from Punjab, Haryana and Himachal Pradesh a direct UAE option without routing through Delhi.
body:
• Air India Express will resume direct flights between Chandigarh and Sharjah from October 26, 2026, operating four times a week.
  • The outbound flight IX453 departs Chandigarh at 1:50 PM and arrives in Sharjah at 4:50 PM; the return IX454 leaves Sharjah at 5:50 PM.
  • One-way fares are listed from around ₹17,000, giving travellers from Punjab, Haryana and Himachal Pradesh an alternative to flying via Delhi.
  • The route was last served until October 2023; its return is part of Air India Express's expanded winter 2026 schedule.

Travellers from the City Beautiful will once again have a direct air link to the UAE. Air India Express is set to resume nonstop services between Chandigarh and Sharjah from October 26, 2026, ending a suspension that began in 2023, according to the airline's current winter schedule.

The service will operate four times a week — on Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday — from Shaheed Bhagat Singh International Airport in Chandigarh to Sharjah International Airport. The outbound flight, IX453, departs Chandigarh at 1:50 PM and arrives in Sharjah at 4:50 PM, with a reported nonstop journey time of four hours and 30 minutes. The return service, IX454, leaves Sharjah at 5:50 PM and lands in Chandigarh at 11:05 PM, a journey of three hours and 45 minutes.

An alternative to the Delhi detour

The resumption matters most for travellers who have spent the last three years routing through Delhi for a direct UAE flight. The airline's current fare listings show one-way fares starting at around ₹17,000, subject to availability — competitive with the Delhi options that Chandigarh-based passengers have been forced onto, without the five-hour road or rail journey to the capital.

The service is expected to benefit travellers from Chandigarh and neighbouring Punjab, Haryana and Himachal Pradesh — a region with deep family, business and tourism ties to the Emirates — as well as passengers seeking onward connections through Sharjah's growing network.

Chandigarh's expanding international map

Once operations begin, Sharjah will join Dubai and Abu Dhabi on the list of direct international connections from Chandigarh. The route's return is part of a broader Air India Express network expansion for the northern winter 2026 season, which also adds Amritsar–Abu Dhabi, Kochi–Bangkok, Mangalore–Ras al Khaimah, Mumbai–Kuwait City and Vishakhapatnam–Bangkok, according to schedule data published by AeroRoutes.

Limited international connectivity has been a long-running focus area for Chandigarh airport, which serves as the international gateway for northern India beyond Delhi. Local industry groups and elected representatives have repeatedly pressed for more overseas services from the airport, arguing that the region's travel demand — driven by a large diaspora, student traffic and business links — justifies it. Each restored route strengthens the airport's case for more, and reduces the region's dependence on the capital's airports.

What's next

Bookings are expected to open through the airline's usual channels ahead of the October 26 launch. Travellers should note that schedule filings can change before the first flight — and that the airline has listed no service on the route between December 1, 2026 and January 31, 2027 in its current filing. For now, though, the direct link is back on the board after nearly three years.
nri_angle: Punjabi diaspora in the UAE gain a direct link home after three years of routing through Delhi — a meaningful improvement for family visits and business travel.
author: Diaspora Desk
